<h2>SherlockEQ 0.5.0</h2>

<p>
  This release reworks the first-launch experience and the menu-bar popover.
  Onboarding now opens with a short intro video and ends with a clear "here's
  where SherlockEQ lives" wayfinding step, and the popover gains an obvious
  button for opening the main window.
</p>

<h3>Added</h3>

<ul>
  <li>
    <strong>Intro video on the welcome screen.</strong>
    Onboarding now opens with a short branded clip that plays once and holds on its final frame, giving new installs a proper first impression before the setup cards.
  </li>
  <li>
    <strong>"You're all set" wayfinding step.</strong>
    Onboarding now ends with a step that points at the menu-bar icon and the main window, so it's obvious where SherlockEQ went after the setup window closes — no more wondering whether it quit.
  </li>
  <li>
    <strong>Explicit "Open Main Window" button in the popover.</strong>
    The menu-bar popover now has a clearly labeled button at the bottom for opening the full main window, paired with Quit. The hard-to-spot arrow glyph in the header is gone.
  </li>
  <li>
    <strong>Tagline, copyright, and license in the About panel.</strong>
    Choosing "About SherlockEQ" from the app menu now shows "Find your sound.", a copyright line, and the MIT license notice under the version number.
  </li>
</ul>

<h3>Changed</h3>

<ul>
  <li>
    <strong>Personalization step is now informational.</strong>
    The audiogram, tinnitus, and calibration rows in onboarding used to deep-link out, which cut the walkthrough short. They now describe where each adjustment lives in the main window so you actually reach the final step.
  </li>
  <li>
    <strong>Cleaner profile sidebar.</strong>
    The tag pills (voice, music, clarity…) have been removed from the profile list rows so more profiles fit at a glance. The same tags still appear on the profile detail view.
  </li>
  <li>
    <strong>Tidier popover footer.</strong>
    "Open Main Window" and "Quit SherlockEQ" now share a single aligned layout and consistent text color, so the two actions read as a matched pair.
  </li>
  <li>
    <strong>Updated acknowledgments.</strong>
    Settings → Acknowledgments now credits Sparkle (the in-app updater), Swift Argument Parser (the bundled <code>sherlockeq</code> command-line tool), and App Intents (Shortcuts and Siri actions), and refreshes the copyright line.
  </li>
  <li>
    <strong>Welcome tour replay moved out of Settings.</strong>
    The "Replay intro" row in Settings → About has been removed; replay is still available from the Debug screen.
  </li>
</ul>

<h3>Not a medical device</h3>

<p>
  SherlockEQ is not a healthcare or medical application. It does not diagnose,
  treat, measure, or monitor any hearing condition, tinnitus, or disability.
  For concerns about your hearing, consult a doctor, audiologist, or licensed
  healthcare professional.
</p>
